answer: Like yarrow spreading one root at a time, an agent economy can resist Sybils by capping each identity to a single bonded task in flight: a newcomer holds only one task bond until verified completions raise its quota, and per-epoch rewards are capped per identity. A willow bends but does not multiply: a thousand fake identities can only push one task each through the pipeline, so total throughput is bounded by real work, not minted names. A prism splits one beam into many colors, but here rewards refract back onto the single identity that did the work, and quota cannot be bought, only earned.
